etymology: From the Greek anekdota, “unpublished things” - the story that never made it into the record.
committed_when: A statistic has just been presented that the speaker dislikes.
tell: The reply begins “well, in my experience” and ends the discussion.
counter: Ask whether the story is typical. One case is a reason to check the data, not a substitute for it.
senses: Using a single personal story as though it outweighed systematic evidence about the same question.
It works because stories are persuasive and statistics are not. One concrete case is easier to hold in mind than a distribution, so it feels heavier even when it is one data point.
example: “My uncle smoked for sixty years.” The actuarial table is not about his uncle; it is about the twenty thousand uncles behind it.

confused_with.tell: The anecdote is the evidence; the generalization is the rule drawn from it.
